A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LEAP work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic graph-classification results, real-world benchmark evaluations, and ablation experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds GIN evaluations, combined-encoding results, and computational timing measurements.

M1.justification: The neighborhood–DECT–projection pipeline and five projection strategies remain unchanged. v2 adds an evaluated variant that concatenates LEAP with LaPE on HIV (Section 4.3); v1 mentioned combining complementary encodings only as future work.

E1.justification: Appendix D adds Roman Empire as a large single-graph runtime evaluation, with 22,662 nodes, 32,927 edges, and 300-dimensional features. The synthetic task, seven classification benchmarks, Alchemy full, and HIV are retained. Further evaluation on non-attributed graph datasets remains future work.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds GIN comparisons using No PE, RWPE, and LaPE alongside LEAP. Section 4.1 also newly reports evaluating RWPE and LaPE on the synthetic task. Existing GCN, GAT, NoMP, and two DECT-budget comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce GIN configurations, concatenated encodings on HIV, and timing protocols separating total training, per-epoch, and preprocessing costs. The existing five-fold cross-validation, Adam optimizer, 100-epoch maximum, and individual 10-dimensional PEs remain. Dimension and budget matching for the concatenated encodings are not specified.

E4.justification: v2 tests complementary information from LEAP and LaPE on HIV, extends the projection-strategy ablation to GIN, and analyzes training and preprocessing overhead in Appendix D. Existing locality, embedding-dimension, direction-count, smoothing, and convergence analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain fixed-seed statements, five-fold cross-validation, the same ± reporting, and identical Appendix B plots showing standard deviations over five runs. v2 introduces no additional run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or changed uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: New GIN result blocks, perfect-accuracy RWPE/LaPE synthetic results, HIV concatenation outcomes, and runtime measurements substantially extend the reported evidence. GAT-HIV results also change: v1 Figure 3 places LaPE above RWPE, whereas v2 Figure S.2 reverses that ordering and places LaPE worst. The reason for those changed values is unspecified. Retained numerical table entries and Alchemy, convergence, and sensitivity plots match.

T1.justification: New Section 3.3 gives O(n^3), O(n^2), and O(n) complexity arguments under different graph assumptions. Equation (4) corrects the ECT indicator intervals, and Equation (3) fixes the LaPE endpoint from i+k to i+k−1. Theorem 1 is retained, with no new expressivity proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and central novelty and performance claims remain. The introduction now explicitly targets geometric graphs and extends the non-informative-feature finding into a claim of applicability to non-attributed graph learning. These are limited scope adjustments to the existing contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the combined HIV encodings as evidence that local and global information complement each other and adds computational-efficiency discussion. It explicitly defers deeper expressivity analysis and notes that theoretical expressivity need not track empirical performance. Existing feature-dependence, approximation, and hyperparameter limitations remain.

D1.justification: The reproducibility statement replaces the anonymous supplementary-code pointer with a named aidos-lab/LEAP GitHub repository. Appendix D supplies timing measurements and identifies neighborhood precomputation as LEAP preprocessing. Hardware, timing units, and detailed timing configurations are not supplied; repository availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 expands the ECT literature discussion with application, review, and generative-work citations, including Cisewski-Kehe et al., Crawford et al., Munch, and Röell and Rieck. Platonov et al. is added for Roman Empire. The central positioning relative to DECT, local ECT, and established PEs remains.

P1.justification: v2 makes copyedits and localized paragraph rewrites throughout the background, methods, and results while retaining the main narrative. It adds a Properties subsection, formally numbers Results, introduces an appendix contents page and Appendix D, and updates publication headers and acknowledgments.

P2.justification: Figure 2 becomes wider and includes combined encodings; v1 Figure 3 is enlarged and split into Figures S.1 and S.2. Tables 4 and S.1 gain GIN blocks, and two timing tables are added. Captions, highlighting, and float placement change, while the method diagram and existing diagnostic graphics remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Corrected mathematical definitions, additional baseline controls, complementary-encoding tests, and timing evidence modestly strengthen v2. However, new reporting inconsistencies limit the gains: Table 4 assigns GIN/Letter-H 62.7±3.4 to LEAP-L, while Table S.1 assigns it to LEAP-F, and the revised HIV/GAT plot contradicts the retained LaPE ranking interpretation. These issues prevent the expanded evidence from establishing a substantial overall improvement.
